guides.summary: Defines the agent-readable Thermite 3 surface and the dependency sequence for the capabilities that follow.
features: Full-word behavioural clauses: requires, ensures, keeps, and measures
Effect rows remain part of function types and precede behavioural clauses
Shared state, resources, interference, and protocols receive distinct surface roles
A staged dependency tree from syntax through protocol-checked concurrency
guides.example:
fn allocate(pages: u64) -> Result<Grant, u64>
  ! write(heap), cost(12 * pages + 40)
  requires pages > 0
  ensures result.is_ok()

guides.summary: Gives effect rows an algebraic meaning so frame conditions and commutation facts are computed rather than maintained as an ad-hoc table.
features: Five basis theories: state, accrues, exception, partiality, and free I/O
Effect entries pair a theory instance with the operations actually used
Computed read/read, read/write, and write/write commutation
User-declared effects compose known theories while retaining named residual trust
guides.example:
effect platform(d) = state(d)
effect journal(d)  = state(d) + exception
effect net(d)      = state(d) + io(sigma_d)

guides.summary: Turns effect rows into checked, region-sensitive upper bounds and rejects unsafe concurrent compositions.
features: Declared shared regions with field-derived containment
Exact body, intrinsic-operation, and transitive callee footprints
Errors for missing effects and loud structured warnings for excess effects
Named concurrent compositions checked with RFC-8 commutation facts
guides.example:
shared scheduler: SchedState
shared clock: TimeState

fn advance() -> u64
  ! write(scheduler), read(clock)
  requires nothing
  ensures result < MAX_SLOTS

guides.summary: Adds lexical lock ownership, protected invariants, ordering, and interrupt masking to shared-state reasoning.
features: Lock declarations connect a lock name to the type whose invariant it guards
owns(lock) exposes acquisition to callers while holding blocks locate it in the body
Rows and lexical holding blocks must agree in both directions
One-lock-by-default ordering and masking rules for handler-visible locks

guides.summary: Introduces resource kinds whose values must be consumed exactly once on every returning path.
features: resource marks non-copyable, non-droppable structs and enums
Resource obligations propagate through fields, variants, and generic containers
Destructuring consumes the container and transfers obligations to its parts
Explicit forget operations make intentional abandonment visible in the effect row
guides.example_label: A grant that must be returned
guides.example:
resource struct Grant { frame: u64, generation: u64 }

fn release(a: Allocator, g: Grant) -> Allocator
  ! pure
  ensures result.free_count == a.free_count + 1

guides.summary: Adds rely-guarantee clauses for concurrent code whose environment may evolve while the function runs.
features: interleaves scopes relational asks and promises clauses
Peer promises must imply the other participant's assumptions
Environment relations must be reflexive and transitive
Postconditions must remain stable under permitted interference

guides.summary: Makes communication protocols resource-typed so endpoint use, branching, and completion are statically disciplined.
features: Protocols describe role-labelled turns ending in end
Endpoint types are named by protocol and role
Branch choices are explicit messages with a named chooser
Resource consumption ties endpoint release to protocol completion
